entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- Amit Kumar Singh,G.A.,Km Astha Hon'ble Raj Beer Singh,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned counsel for the informant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

2. The present bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in case crime No. 223/2023,
under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, police station Ekdil, District Etawah with the prayer to enlarge the applicant on bail.
3. It has been argued by learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant-accused is innocent and he has not committed any offence.
Applicant is husband of deceased.
The marriage of deceased with applicant has taken place about three years prior to the incident and out of that marriage, they have two children.

After marriage for a period of three years, there had no complaint against the Gaurav vs State Of U.P. on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69156889/
1 applicant regarding dowry demand and harassment of deceased.
It was submitted that entire family of applicant was named in the first information report.
Only general allegations of dowry demand and harassment of deceased have been levelled against the applicant and co-accused persons and that no specific role has been assigned to the applicant.
It was further submitted that in fact deceased was insisting to visit her sister in Rajasthan and when applicant refused, she has committed suicide.
After the incident, applicant has given information to the police and thereafter inquest proceedings were conducted.
At the time of inquest proceedings, applicant as well as father of deceased were present.
The allegation that after the incident, applicant has run away from the spot is wholly false.
The first information report was lodged on the next day by the mother of deceased.
In postmortem report, except ligature mark, no other injury has been shown on the body of deceased and cause of death has been shown as ante-mortem hanging.
Both the minor children of deceased are being maintained and looked-after by the mother of applicant.

Lastly, it was submitted that the applicant is in judicial custody since 26.09.2023, having no criminal history, and that in case applicant is enlarged on bail, the applicant will not misuse the liberty of bail.

4. Learned A.G.A. as well as learned counsel for the informant have opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that deceased has suffered unnatural death within a period of three years of her marriage.
In postmortem report, cause of death has been shown ante-mortem hanging but viscera report is yet to be received.
Referring to the statements of witnesses, it was submitted that there is evidence that deceased was being harassed on account of dowry.

5. Considering the submissions of learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusations, period of custody and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on the merits, a case for bail is made out.
Hence, the bail application is hereby allowed.

6. Let the applicant Gaurav involved in the aforesaid crime be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two local sureties each of the like amount to the satisfaction of court concerned subject to the following conditions:
i.
The applicant shall not tamper with the evidence during trial.
ii. The applicant shall not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witnesses.
iii. The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
iv. The applicant shall not try to contact, threat or otherwise influence the complainant or any of the witness of the case.
7. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the court concerned shall be at liberty to cancel the bail of applicant, in accordance with law.

Order Date :- 13.5.2024 Anand  Gaurav vs State Of U.P. on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69156889/
